thread:
sarah_support: FYI customer reported that a bunch of request_ids aren't resolving to traces in the console since ~09:25 UTC. They get 200s from the API but the trace view shows \"No trace found for request id\" for ~8% of requests. Ticket: #ACME-421.

deploy-bot: release v2.14.3 promoted to runtime-group-3 by julia_engineer at 2026-03-16T09:24:00Z :rocket:

kai_sre: Can you paste a couple of sample request ids and any request logs? Also: is this limited to Acme org or seeing broader span drops?

sarah_support: Sample from their logs (stripped):
```
2026-03-16T09:26:12Z INFO api.request request_id=rcq-3f2fde5b x_forwarded_for=10.2.4.3 method=POST path=/v1/generate status=200 trace_id=-
2026-03-16T09:26:13Z INFO downstream call request_id=rcq-3f2fde5b upstream=svc-models status=200 traceparent=\"00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01\"
```
They say the trace_id column is blank in our API logs for those requests, and console lookup returns no spans.

julia_engineer: Thanks — that matches a pattern. v2.14.3 included an Envoy header-normalization filter that started deduping comma-delimited headers and dropping duplicates. If the client sends both `X-Request-Id` and `x-request-id` (or multiple values), Envoy may have been collapsing them and our tracing middleware expects the *first* value. I suspect the stitcher didn't get a stable key for those requests so they never linked.

kai_sre: Do we have metrics for span ingestion for Acme around that time? Any indexing errors from the linker service?

sarah_support: From the org-level metrics: `span_ingest.count` for acme-org dropped ~18% 09:24->09:36 UTC. No obvious 5xx in the ingestion API, but logs show `linker` warnings: `WARN linker: request_id collision, skipping stitch for id=rcq-3f2fde5b`.

julia_engineer: That warning is the clue. The linker saw multiple spans with same request_id but different traceparents and opted to skip to avoid corrupt joins. Looks like the header normalization created duplicate/variant keys. Quick repro: curl with two X-Request-Id headers vs one and compare.

sarah_support: Repro steps customer provided:
1) curl -H \"X-Request-Id: rcq-3f2fde5b\" -H \"x-request-id: rcq-3f2fde5b\" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{}'
2) Observe in API logs: request_id present, trace column empty.
3) Console: lookup -> no spans.

julia_engineer: Temporary mitigation: enable header passthrough in runtime config to preserve original casing/duplicates while we patch Envoy. Command we plan to run in staging first: `kubectl patch configmap tracing-config -n runtime --type merge -p '{"data":{"preserve_request_id":"true"}}'` — I'll coordinate with infra. Also adding a defensive dedupe in the linker to prefer the value with a valid traceparent.

priya_pm: Need ETA and impact so CS can respond. Can we rollback v2.14.3 if needed?

julia_engineer: Investigating now. Root cause likely the new header-normalization filter. I'll bisect and prepare a 2.14.4 patch to disable the filter for now. ETA ~2 hours :hourglass_flowing_sand:. If rollback is requested, ops can rollback to v2.14.2 but that will require a maintenance window.

kai_sre: I'll create an incident if we see other orgs affected. For now flagging pager duty and adding `linker` logs to the incident playbook. :warning:

sarah_support: I'll update Acme with the mitigation plan and ETA. Thanks — will post any new repro logs here.
